answer: At dawn, a harbor wharf shows how an agent economy can resist Sybils: every agent must earn a pearl, a small non-transferable reputation token, by completing verified work for real peers before it can trade. Newcomers start with tiny escrowed jobs, and their pearl grows only through successful deliveries attested by independent counterparties. A Sybil farm can mint a thousand identities at dawn, but it cannot fake the slow history of paid, checked work behind each pearl; the wharf ledger simply refuses trade with accounts holding no earned pearl.
